marina: Running a perf sweep on the 8-GPU config with tensor-slicing + pipeline stages. I see ~20% throughput drop when switching from FP16 to mixed-int8 profile under TP=2/PP=2. Logs attached below.
marina: Quick summary: single-step latency stable, but sustained throughput falls and device utilization drops on rank 2/3. All-reduce shows spikes.
marina: nvprof excerpt:
```
GPU 0 util: 92% | GPU 1 util: 90% | GPU 2 util: 38% | GPU 3 util: 35%
AllReduce (ring) latency: avg 1.9ms -> spikes 9-12ms at sequence boundary
KV cache memcpy peaks on GPU 2 at 4.5ms
```
marina: Batching heuristics: batch_size=16, auto-batcher enabled, dynamic batching window=15ms. When I force smaller batches (8) throughput recovers a bit but not fully.
ashok: Interesting. Do we see imbalance in token distribution across pipeline stages? That'd explain low util on ranks 2/3.
jude: Can you paste the schedule/partition? Might be uneven micro-batching between TP shards.
marina: Partition: model split: [layers 0-14]->rank0/1, [15-29]->rank2/3; TP=2 within each stage. Micro-batches=4. Seems balanced on paper.
marina: Profiling shows that when INT8 kernels are selected on TP shards the GEMM times are lower but the commute to allreduce & CUDA memcpy interleave badly. The runtime picks INT8 matmul kernels on even ranks and FP16 on odd ranks due to kernel selection threshold for sequence length.
kai: That kernel heterogeneity is a red flag. Mixing kernel precision across ranks can increase comm/compute imbalance because different ranks finish compute at different times.
sara: Any evidence of numerical instability when forcing uniform int8? We need to know if it's safe to standardize kernels across ranks.
jude: Also could be KV cache alignment: if some ranks serialize KV flushes at different points that triggers extra barriers.
marina: I tested forcing INT8 everywhere (runtime flag --force-precision int8). Throughput improved vs mixed, but output logits diverged ~1e-3 in topk scores for long contexts. Not catastrophic, but we have a regression test that fails.
ashok: So two problems: perf regression from mixed kernels + comm spikes, and quality regression when forcing int8 globally.
kai: For comm overlap: can we reorder pre/post allreduce so KV memcpy is not blocking? Maybe schedule async copy + compute overlap window
marina: I tried async copies + prefetching KV into pinned host memory. Reduced memcpy peaks but allreduce latency still spikes at sequence boundaries.
ashok: Looks like the allreduce implementation (ring) has an O(N) step that synchronizes at micro-batch end. On variable micro-batch timing that hits worst-case.
ashok: Suggestion: try toggling NCCL algorithm (tree vs ring) and tune chunk size. Also ensure NCCL_ASYNC_PROGRESS=1 for overlap.
marina: Quick test: NCCL_ALGO=tree + chunk=8MB reduced allreduce spikes by ~30% and smoothed util across GPUs. Throughput up ~9% but still below FP16 baseline.
jude: That indicates kernel selection heterogeneity still matters. If some ranks use slower FP16 GEMMs while others use faster int8, the advantage is lost.
kai: Potential fixes:
- Align kernel selection policy across TP shards (force same kernel family per layer across TP)
- Add runtime check to avoid mixing int8 and fp16 for same logical layer across ranks
- Improve batching policy to prefer micro-batch counts that even out compute finish times
- Adaptive NCCL chunking at runtime triggered by observed imbalances

sara: From ops side, deploying a change that forces int8 everywhere will need validation (quality + fallback). Can we add an automatic fallback to FP16 when eval detects divergence?
marina: I ran a quality eval with the int8-only run: perplexity up 0.8% on long-context eval set; certain syntactic completions degrade. We can add quant-scale calibration for TP shards to reduce drift.
ashok: The quant scaling per TP shard could be slightly misaligned due to different FP accumulation ranges. Maybe separator step: share calibration stats across TP ranks during model init.
marina: Implementation note: we can broadcast scale tensors during init via the control plane before serving. That would force consistent quant params.
kai: Also consider mixed accumulation: use INT8 kernels but FP32 accumulation in reduce to avoid drift. Some kernels support that.
jude: Short-term mitigation: set kernel-selection to prefer FP16 when PP>1 and batch window>10ms. Longer-term: kernel homogeneity + shared quant stats.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for runtime patch kernel-selection-homogenize on 4 nodes.
sara: I'll watch SLOs. If we see tail latency regressions, we'll roll back.
marina: Next actions I'll take:
1) implement broadcast of quant scales during init (PR later today)
2) add runtime guard to avoid mixed-kernel selection across TP shards
3) test NCCL tree + adaptive chunking in perf harness

ashok: Thanks Marina. If you want I'll pair on the PR for kernel-selection logic.
marina: Appreciate it. I'll post PR link when ready and attach updated perf graphs.
ashok: 👍
